summary.text: Tommy Tuberville is Alabama's senior U.S. senator and a former college football head coach, including at Auburn University from 1999 to 2008.

First elected in 2020 when he defeated Sen. Doug Jones, he is now the Republican nominee for governor, running on an "Alabama First Agenda" of cutting taxes and government waste, expanding school choice, protecting Second Amendment rights and tougher border enforcement.

paragraphs.text: Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, and earned a B.S. in physical education from Southern State College (now Southern Arkansas University) in 1976.

He was head football coach at Ole Miss from 1995 to 1998, Auburn from 1999 to 2008, Texas Tech from 2010 to 2012 and Cincinnati from 2013 to 2016, a coaching career of about forty years, and worked as a broadcaster for ESPN in 2017.

In 2020, in his first political campaign, Tuberville was elected to the U.S. Senate, defeating incumbent Democrat Doug Jones. He announced in 2025 that he would run for governor, and he and Jones won their parties' nominations in May 2026.
He lives in Auburn, Alabama, with his wife, Suzanne.
